rules.name: The Locate Code Rule
rules.body: A utility color always travels with its dash pattern and its name. Color alone never carries meaning, and the four colors never color text, fills or backgrounds; the one exception is the selected bill's 3px bottom rule in its utility color.

rules.name: The Hatching Rule
rules.body: Tone comes from 45° hatching (1px ink at 10% every 8 to 9px). Never a tinted fill.

rules.name: The Size Is Billing Rule
rules.body: Share figures outweigh the H1, and what the bill's owner is owed back is the largest number on the sheet.

rules.name: The Lane Label Rule
rules.body: Each lane label sits in the rightmost hall gap clear of every drop, measured from its rendered width, haloed in sheet highlight so drops pass under it; fall back to beside the meters.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The House Ledger"**

There is one ledger for the house, kept in one of four hands. **Statement** is the bank's printout: a grey page, white sheets, a single blue, and IBM Plex Mono on every figure, date and label, so the screen reads like the portal your utility company wishes it had. **Peach** is the book kept on the porch: cream paper under a striped peach awning with a scalloped hem, Fraunces for display, Karla for body text, and Courier Prime typing the figures in. **Japandi** is the kakeibo kept on an oak desk: linen paper, washi panels, sumi ink, one dyed-indigo accent, Zen Kaku Gothic New for body and titles, M PLUS 1 Code for every figure, and a noren along the top of the page: an indigo cloth in seigaiha waves hung from a 3px oak rod. **Sheet** is the house's own drafting sheet: the public site's world (see Public Site: The Drafting Sheet, below) worn by a household. Ink on a cool white sheet under a 24px grid, ink as the one accent with the highlighter as its wash, Archivo set wide and heavy for titles, Martian Mono condensed for every figure, square everything and 1.5px ink frames. All four share the same components, the same layout and the same rules for money. The theme changes the hand, never the record.

The feel is **friendly and sturdy**. Surfaces are flat paper divided by hairline rules, with comfortable tap targets and soft corners. Nothing floats, glows or competes with the numbers. The density is that of a well-kept statement: a summary strip of three figures, then ruled tables that reflow into small ledger cards on a phone. Most visits happen on a phone, cold, once a month, so every screen opens with what's owed and by when, and offers one obvious thing to do.

Theme differences are design, not inconsistency. Never "fix" one theme toward another. Fraunces and the awning are deliberate, and so are japandi's lighter weights and its one rail, and the sheet's square corners, grid and ink frames.
keyCharacteristics: Four themes, one component set, switched by `<html data-theme>` from the household's settings.
Every number, date, count and section label is set in the theme's ledger monospace with tabular figures.
One accent per theme (statement blue, deep peach, aizome indigo, and in sheet ink itself with the highlighter as its wash). Peach adds periwinkle as a quiet second voice.
Green, red and amber (sage, rose and butter in peach; moss, persimmon and ochre in japandi; the sheet's own inked steps) mean paid, unpaid and due soon, and nothing else.
Flat surfaces with hairline borders. Shadows only on things that float.
Statement supports dark mode. Peach, japandi and sheet are light-only on purpose.
One signature move per theme: peach's awning, japandi's noren, the sheet's 24px drafting grid on the page. Statement has none.

rules.name: The Reserved Semantics Rule
rules.body: Green, red and amber (sage, rose and butter) belong to paid, unpaid and due soon (overdue reads as unpaid). Never use them for decoration, branding or generic success and error. The one exception is flash messages, which borrow the paid and unpaid washes for ok and err.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each theme has exactly one interactive color. If something is clickable and not a status, it is the accent or it is ink. In japandi that color is aizome indigo, and it is interactive-only: no heading, figure, fill or decoration borrows it. In sheet the accent is ink itself, so clickable and ink are the same thing. Series colors are data and never clickable; the legend toggle that shows or hides a line is ink, with the series drawn in its swatch.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: The sheet's one colour outside status and charts, the yellow highlighter, marks selected text only. It never fills a chosen card, a pressed toggle, a banner or a hover; those take the ink border and the 3px ink rule instead.

rules.name: The Calm Red Rule
rules.body: Unpaid and overdue use the soft wash with colored text, never a solid red block. Owing money is information, not an alarm.

rules.name: The Change It Once Rule
rules.body: Theme colors live in `lib/theme-tokens.ts`. Emails import them, and `npm run verify` (the `tokens` suite) fails if `app/globals.css`, this file's frontmatter or `.impeccable/design.json` disagrees. Change the module first, then the others.

rules.name: The Ledger Face Rule
rules.body: Every number, amount, date, count and section label is set in the theme's ledger monospace with tabular figures (the `.figure` / `.eyebrow` voice). Prose never is. If a value can be added up or put on a calendar, it is monospace.

rules.name: The Right-Edge Rule
rules.body: Amount columns are right-aligned so the decimal points line up.

rules.name: The Scale Leads Rule
rules.body: Japandi never reaches for a heavier weight to make a thing important. The page title is 1.6x body at 500, summary figures are 500 where the other themes use 600, and the small step (eyebrows, table heads) is 0.78x body. Size and air carry the hierarchy; 700 exists in the face but the system does not use it.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: The sheet's hierarchy is width as much as weight. Words that name (titles 108%, the wordmark 118%, buttons 106%) go wide in Archivo; things that measure (figures, eyebrows, table heads, chips, 87.5%) go narrow in Martian Mono. Nothing on the sheet is set at the faces' default width.

rules.name: The No Sideways Scroll Rule
rules.body: A phone never scrolls horizontally. New tables join the `.table-stack` system with their own grid-template-areas instead of overflowing.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Panels, cards, tables and buttons have no shadow at rest or on hover. If it doesn't float over other content, it doesn't cast a shadow.

dos: Do set every amount, date, count and eyebrow in the theme's ledger mono with tabular figures, and right-align amount columns.

Do build every new surface from the shared component classes (`.panel`, `.btn*`, `.tag*`, `.due-*`, `.field-*`, `.data-table`, `.eyebrow`, `.figure`, `.panel-primary`, `.choice-card`) so all four themes come for free. A theme varies tokens and a few signature rules, not markup.

Do add theme differences as token overrides under `[data-theme="peach"]`, `[data-theme="japandi"]` or `[data-theme="sheet"]`, keeping peach's rounder radii, pill tags, bolder eyebrows, Fraunces titles and awning, japandi's crisper radii, square tags, the PAID seal, 500-weight titles and figures, and the noren, and the sheet's zero radii, 24px grid, 1.5px ink frames, ringed tags, wide Archivo titles and condensed Martian figures.
Do give each screen exactly one primary button, and keep its tap target at 36px or more. The small button is for inline row actions.
Do make every new table a `.table-stack` with named grid areas for its phone layout.
Do pair every figure with a plain-words caption in muted ink ("from 2 roommates", "nothing due from you").
Do check new color pairs in all four themes and in statement dark, and keep text at 4.5:1 or better. Record peach's, japandi's and sheet's measured ratios in Colors > Contrast.
Do change a theme color in `lib/theme-tokens.ts` first, then mirror it in `app/globals.css`, this file and `.impeccable/design.json` until `npm run verify -- tokens` passes.
Do give a chart a legend of real buttons, a point shape per series, and a table that says the same thing in figures. Take series colors from `--series-N` in slot order.
Do ask with `ConfirmButton` before anything that removes, sends or reassigns, and never with the browser's `confirm()`. Put any other modal content in `Dialog`; never hand-roll an overlay.
Do leave an empty cell empty. No "—" placeholders in tables or figures.

Do keep japandi's one accent interactive-only: aizome indigo for links, focus, selection, checked controls and the primary button, and nothing else. Mount any new japandi flourish on the noren or not at all.
Do let the global reduced-motion rule handle motion. Never re-enable animation with `!important` under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do keep the sheet's highlighter for text selection only. A chosen or pressed thing in sheet takes the ink border and the 3px ink rule along its bottom.
Do frame exactly one panel per sheet page with `.panel-primary`, and draw a neutral chip in sheet as a ringed box, never a tinted one.
donts: Don't "fix" one theme toward another. Fraunces, the awning, the pills and the warm palette are intentional; so are japandi's lighter weights, square tags, sealed PAID and wave noren, and the sheet's hard corners, heavy frames, grid and black-ink accent. None of it is slop.
Don't give peach, japandi or sheet a dark mode. All three are light-only on purpose; a sumi-ink dark variant for japandi is deferred, not planned, and a sheet of paper has no dark side.

Don't use green, red or amber (sage, rose or butter; moss, persimmon or ochre) for anything but paid, unpaid and due soon, and don't add a second accent to statement or japandi. Series colors stay inside charts.
Don't fill a block with solid red for an unpaid or overdue state. Use the wash and colored text.

Don't add shadows, gradients or glows to panels, cards or buttons at rest. The awning stripes and the sheet's grid lines are the only gradients in the system; the noren's waves are the one other gradient; the PAID seal is the only ringed tag outside sheet, where every tag is ringed.
Don't give the sheet a shadow anywhere, a radius anywhere, or a second accent. Its dialog and phone menu are framed, not lifted.
Don't let a phone layout scroll sideways, or set an input below 16px on a phone.
Don't spell the product name or domain in UI or email. Read them from `BRAND`.
Don't put a logo in the nav. The household name is the wordmark.
Don't hard-code a color in an email template. Take it from `lib/theme-tokens.ts`.
